subject: 30 TGP2 refusals: exact cause is 4KiB TGP1 code cap; fix in pipeline_format.h, lowering L2 rebuild needed
body:
Root cause of the 30 generic "unsupported TGP2 native pipeline or resource manifest requirements" refusals is now exact, not a mystery feature. In metal/tegu/pipeline_format.h parse2 used TEGU_PIPELINE_MAX_CODE=4096u (the legacy TGP1 cap) on the TGP2 code length. Real CoreRE/UI kernels emit Mali code 4864..14848 bytes, so the compiler constructs a valid TGP2 packet and its own parser returns -2 at the header check.

Evidence: gdb break at tegu_pipeline_parse2 in frozen compiler ea4454b7 on the failing SPIR-V; return -2. Dumped 14 failing real packets (15 generic rows; one did not reach the breakpoint and is marked separately) from evidence-current-ea4454b7-3fa3020d/compute_fc_p0_v2 and evidence-current-ea4454b7-1e6cc1e2/compute_fc_p1. With the fixed parser all 14 parse rc0; code bytes: 14848,7680,5504,8576,4864,7936,6656,4864,5632,5504,4736,7040,9600,5760; manifest counts 4..11; local1,1,1. Histogram = 14/14 captured refusals are TGP2 code >4096 (the 15th needs its own capture; no other parser field failed in these).

FIX (applied in my owned pipeline_format.h):
#define TEGU_PIPELINE2_MAX_CODE (1u<<20)
and parse2 uses it; TGP1 parse still uses TEGU_PIPELINE_MAX_CODE=4096. Added a 5000-byte TGP2 parser test; C suite release+ASan PASS. TGP2 header/manifest and native ABI unchanged. This does not affect TGP1.
This needs a lowering L2 Mesa rebuild to put the new header into libnord2_mali_runtime.so; I cannot rebuild Mesa. Lowering/root: please include it, then re-run the 30 cases and post the histogram. The generic compiler message can remain until then, but the reason is deterministic. No phone/native/device.
